🚂 Turkey's railways · 1858 → 2026

Anatolia's first train ran in 1858, on the British-built İzmir–Aydın line. Until 1918 the network grew through foreign concessions: the German-backed Anatolian Railway reached Ankara (1892) and Konya (1896), then the Baghdad Railway crossed the Taurus. The Republic then built its own lines east and to the Black Sea coal: Sivas, Zonguldak, Erzurum (1939). The Kars line in the far east is older: the Russian Empire laid Kars–Sarıkamış in 1899 and a narrow-gauge line on to Erzurum in 1917; Turkey rebuilt it to standard gauge in 1949–1961, and the map dates it from the first track. In blue, the high-speed lines, from Ankara–Eskişehir in 2009 to Çerkezköy–Kapıkule, opened on 9 October 2026.

📊 Data: OpenHistoricalMap + OpenStreetMap (ODbL); opening years set section by section from Turkish Wikipedia's list of railway lines and Wikidata. Kilometres are line length (about 9,500 km for TCDD in 2024). A suspended service counts as a closure (Kars–Gyumri, 1993). Sections without a sourced date are left out.
🌍 Land: Natural Earth
